gloss: empty · hollow · the sky — and, in Buddhist texts, emptiness (śūnyatā)
formNote: The Shuowen glosses 空 as 竅, “an opening”, with 穴 as the meaning and 工 as the sound. Mojidata IDS breaks 穴 further into 宀 + 儿. Unihan gives two fanqie, 苦紅 (level tone, kōng) and 苦貢 (departing tone, kòng, “to leave empty; free time”).
summary: A hollow, an opening, the open sky. Buddhist translators chose it for śūnyatā, the emptiness of independent existence, after an earlier period of reading that idea through 無 (see 無’s card, 本無 → 空).
placement: On the axis below the sphere, at the higher of the system's two lower equilibria (x = y = 0, z ≈ −0.838): a still point beneath the whole flow, with the hollow tube above it left empty. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

satellites.title: Form Is Emptiness
satellites.evidence: Xuanzang’s Heart Sutra: 色不異空，空不異色；色即是空，空即是色 — “form is not other than emptiness, emptiness is not other than form; form is emptiness, emptiness is form.” 空 had meant a hollow or open space; here it names śūnyatā, the lack of independent existence (svabhāva) in whatever arises from conditions.
satellites.caveat: Emptiness in this sense is not nothingness; the tradition treats reading it as nihilism as a basic error.

satellites.title: An Opening, and Two Tones
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen: 空，竅也, “an opening”, from 穴 (cave) with 工 giving the sound. Unihan records two fanqie, 苦紅 and 苦貢: the level-tone kōng, “empty”, and the departing-tone kòng, “to leave empty”, a derivation by tone like 量’s and 為’s.
